description:
Analyse FAILED SimplifyQA executions — test cases, suites, execution plans — together. ANALYSE: `codes` (TC-123 / SU-123 / PL-123, each → its latest execution) and/or `executionIds` (id or EX code); `code` / `executionId` work too. Returns an `analysisId` (FA-…), a card (scope, failures by category with counts and %, patterns, failed test cases) and evidence per pattern.
VIEW: pass `analysisId` (no re-fetch) with `view` ("consolidated" | "suite"), `suiteId`, `pattern` (n or [n,…]), `category` or `page`.
REVIEW: `{ analysisId, review: true, page? }` — every failed test case, as many per page as fit 18 images: its failed step and the same step in the last pass at the same detail (expected / actual, test data, full API, locator, logs), with every screenshot of both steps, the baseline of both runs and the element thumbnail.
Images: the failed screenshot is this run. The baseline is the execution-time reference page with the target element boxed in red. The thumbnail is the target element as recorded. Same page as the baseline but the element missing or different from the thumbnail means the element or locator changed. A different page (error, blank, another screen) means the flow did not reach it. Recorded images show recording-time data: compare layout and element, not values.

ANALYSE also takes `context` ({ plannedChanges?: string[], knownOutages?: [{ from, to, note? }] } — what the user says changed or was down; shown to you, never applied by code) and `screenText` (default true: read the failed screenshot text).
The analysis carries an application profile: START your first response by stating the application domain you infer from it (name, confidence, flows, terms) — never guess silently — and pass it as `domain` to `failure_analysis_classify`. A pattern may carry a "Previously classified by a reviewer" line.
PARALLEL REVIEW: a client that can run parallel agents may split the review pages across them — each worker calls `failure_analysis({ analysisId, review: true, page: n })` for its own page numbers and returns one line per test case: screen shows · changed vs last pass · category · confidence · reason — then the coordinator classifies once.
Do this, in order:
(1) Read the card and the evidence.
(2) Page the remaining groups with `pattern:[…]` exactly as the card's "Next:" line says, until every pattern's evidence has been read.
(3) Review every failed test case with `review: true`, following its "Next:" line until done: compare the last passed step with the failed step (data, API, locator, logs, version, every image) and state what changed and what stayed the same.
(4) Call `failure_analysis_classify` ONCE with a verdict for ALL groups (`splitOut` test cases whose review shows another cause; `mergeInto` groups that share one).
(5) Reply starting with the classified card exactly as returned (same tables and rows, never reworded), then Why / Fix per pattern from the evidence.
Categories (exactly three): APP_DEFECT (Application Failures) — the application does something wrong with an unchanged test and unchanged data, or the application / a service is down or unreachable (HTTP 404/5xx page, subtype "environment"). AUTOMATION_DATA (Automation Script / Test Data Failures) — script, locator, timing/synchronisation, test data, configuration, device, a manual stop, or the application changed on purpose (screen, label, flow, rule, expected value) so the test is outdated (subtype "intended change"). UNCLASSIFIED (Unclassified / Investigation Required) — the evidence does not decide it; rootCause is then the reason / the missing evidence. "Element not found" with no other evidence is UNCLASSIFIED.
A "suggested:" category is a rule hint, not a verdict. A verdict shown as "(not reviewed)" is low confidence: no test case of that pattern was reviewed. For Excel / PDF files use `failure_analysis_export`.

analysisId.description: VIEW an existing analysis (FA-…) instead of analysing again.

category.description: With analysisId: only this category (APP_DEFECT | AUTOMATION_DATA | UNCLASSIFIED).

codes.description: TC-123 / SU-123 / PL-123 — each analysed at its latest execution.

compareWithLastPass.description: Compare each pattern's failure with the last pass (default true).

context.description: Analyse: what the user says changed or was down — plannedChanges (<=10 strings of <=200 chars) and knownOutages (<=10 { from, to, note? } ISO times). Shown to you as evidence; never applied by code.

executionId.description: One execution id or EX code (same as executionIds:[id]).

executionIds.description: Execution ids or EX codes — only these executions.

includeImages.description: Return failed / last-passed screenshot pairs for the patterns shown as inline images (default true; analyse and view). Set false for text only.

maxLogLines.description: Cap logs per step — the lines nearest the failure are kept (default 30).

page.description: With analysisId: page of the groups list (or of the review with review:true).

pattern.description: With analysisId: these pattern groups, with full evidence.

review.description: With analysisId: review EVERY failed test case, as many per page as fit 18 images (failed step vs the last pass, with every image of both). Follow its "Next:" line until done.

runId.description: Same as executionId (kept for older calls).

screenText.description: Analyse: read text from the failed screenshots (default true). Set false to skip.

suiteId.description: With analysisId: only this suite (SU-12 or 12). Without it: same as code SU-<id>.

tcId.description: Test case id — same as code TC-<id>.

view.description: View: one list (default) or per suite.

name: failure_analysis
title: Analyse failed SimplifyQA test cases, suites or execution plans
